title: sync.recordOpen turns true before the cloud record is drawn, so a render in between can count the phone's copy under the cloud's name
evidence: Done: ShownRecord.open is now the shown session's record drawn (ShownRecord.open(shown:drawn:), nil-guarded), and RootView's countable reads it, so the draw, not the open, flips the key and takes the count, even at an equal epoch. sync.recordOpen and its other readers are unchanged. The Disconnect side of the same window: S73. From the S43 work (PR 1685). ios/HealthRoadmap/Sync/CloudSync.swift:368-372 runs send(.opened…) inside store.handOver's decide, which sets connection.shownSession, so recordOpen (:57) is true. Only then does ios/HealthRoadmap/MyData/RecordStore+Source.swift:172-173 run await self.draw(view), and draw awaits the engine actor (MyData/RecordStore.swift:235 engine.screen). A render in that window builds ShownRecord with open: true and the phone copy's epoch; ShownRecord's doc names the window (Reminders/ReminderScheduler.swift:191-194). RootView's onChange(of: shownRecord) (App/RootView.swift:121) runs recordChanged (:203), and countable (:214, App/FirstRun.swift:121 Cover.countable) is true, so takeCount (:217-220) can store the phone copy's eraseEpoch under the cloud's source. Every first connect and provider switch passes through this window; PR 1685 (S43) narrowed it only for the launch finish. Design note first; touches sync and store. Suggested fix: Cover.countable also requires the drawn record to be the shown session's, e.g. store.source.session == sync.connection.shownSession (source.session is already read at MyData/RecordStore+Source.swift:162). Test: connect, a render between .opened and the draw, no count taken until the cloud record is drawn.
